edits.old: Treat TCMalloc and ExpressPlan as changes at different layers when analyzing WiredTiger performance: the former changes allocation and memory reuse, while the latter reduces query planning work before storage-engine access. Neither source establishes a replacement of WiredTiger’s on-disk structures. (medium confidence)
edits.new: TCMalloc and ExpressPlan are changes at different layers: the 8.0 TCMalloc upgrade changes the memory allocator's caches (per-CPU instead of per-thread, to reduce fragmentation), while ExpressPlan lets a limited set of queries bypass regular query planning and read directly from the storage engine. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/tcmalloc-performance.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/engineering/mongodb-8-0-improving-performance-avoiding-regressions ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md

So, a tiger team member did an experiment to bypass the entire query planner and hard code reading from the storage engine.

edits.old: TCMalloc per-CPU mode relies on Linux restartable sequences (rseq) to update CPU-local allocation structures without locking. MongoDB documents fallback to per-thread caches when glibc registers rseq first. (high confidence)

If another application, such as the glibc library, registers an rseq structure before TCMalloc, TCMalloc can't use rseq. Without rseq, TCMalloc uses per-thread caches, which are used by the legacy TCMalloc version.

edits.old: MongoDB 8.0 upgraded TCMalloc from per-thread to per-CPU caches on supported platforms, with the stated aims of reducing fragmentation and improving resilience under high-stress workloads. This is a server allocator change that also affects storage-engine allocations. (high confidence)
edits.new: MongoDB 8.0 upgraded TCMalloc from per-thread to per-CPU caches, to reduce memory fragmentation and make the database more resilient to high-stress workloads; the updated TCMalloc is supported on x86_64 and ARM64 Linux only. It is a server-wide allocator change; MongoDB engineering notes that allocator fragmentation affects memory used by the WiredTiger cache. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/tcmalloc-performance.md ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/WT-6175
